text:
mike: Quick perf dump from today's host ingress pass — full end-to-end profile (http/gRPC) uploaded: https://ci.internal/flame/3890123456
olivia: skimmed the flamegraphs — biggest wall is tokenization + parse framing, not the model hot path. tokenize::split and parse::frame_deserialize peaks at ~0.75s
kai: noticed KV cache churn aligned with those peaks. small streaming chunks (<=1KB) seem to evict a lot of tiny prefixes from kvcache :thinking: could be our prefix canonicalization alloc pattern
sophie: do we have gRPC writev stats? small writes + TCP push might be amplifying syscall overhead. also curious about header parsing cost for http1 vs http2
mike: pasted a short trace and example logs below:
```text
WRT writev: 42 calls in 1s, median 24us, p95 120us
parse: frame_deserialize (allocs=312, bytes=48KB) per-request median
kv: cache_hit=0.62 cache_miss=0.38 hot_shard=idx7
```
olivia: thanks. two angles: 1) reduce tokenization copies (avoid intermediate string joins), 2) change chunking heuristic to prefer 4-8KB slices for interactive streams
kai: proto suggestion: when request.size < 8KB, buffer until either 8KB or end-of-message OR 8ms timeout. minimizes writev count, increases batching w/o harming latency
sophie: can we add a quick microbenchmark? e.g. run 10k simulated small-utterances with old vs buffered chunker, measure syscalls + p50/p95 stall
mike: started an A/B canary on two hosts: host-a (current) host-b (buffered chunking + tokenization tweak). initial telemetry (10m): host-b reduced writev by 68%, p50 ingress parse CPU down 18%
perf-bot: perf-regression-checker: Alert suppressed (improvement) — CPU cost delta: -17.8% (CI: synthetic load), KV miss ratio unchanged within noise
olivia: KV miss unchanged is expected — we reduced syscall overhead but still doing same logical kvcache lookups. next step: avoid canonicalization mallocs in kvcache lookup (fast path)
kai: here's a tiny patch snippet that inlines the key-hash for small tokens to avoid heap allocs:
```cpp
// fast path: small key inlined into 16-byte buffer
if (len <= 16) { memcpy(inline_buf, src, len); hash = hash_inline(inline_buf, len); } else { hash = hash_heap(src, len); }
```
mike: deployed patch to canary host-b as well. initial numbers look promising but want another hour of steady-state before rolling wider
sophie: also tested HTTP/2 path — multiplexing reduces writev, but header parsing still expensive for ~40B custom headers. can we fold header-check into the existing framing state machine to save one pass?
olivia: agree. small win but cumulative. I'll file a tiny follow-up: reduce header copy and reuse header buffer across streams
kai: one more oddity: when kvcache hot_shard == idx7 we see a tail latency bump. maybe shard imbalance under certain request keys. adding extra shard bits reduced p99 on host-b in the run
mike: plan: 1) keep buffered chunking + tokenization tweak on canary for 2h 2) push inline-key-hash and shard tweak to experiment branch 3) add microbench harness for http1 vs http2 header parsing
sophie: +1. also add a log flag to trace writev coalescing decisions (off by default)
perf-bot: scheduled postmortem job: run nightly synthetic with 1M tiny requests across 8 hosts to validate long-tail regressions
mike: cool. if no regressions after 2h I'll start a staggered rollout (10% -> 33% -> 100%). updating the rollout doc now. :thumbsup:
